mission_09: Online meta-learning addresses the scenario where tasks arrive sequentially over time, and the model must continuously adapt and improve. Unlike batch meta-learning that trains on a fixed set of tasks, online meta-learning must balance adaptation to the current task with maintaining knowledge from previous tasks. The key metric is regret: the difference between the cumulative loss of the online algorithm and the best fixed model in hindsight. A good online meta-learning algorithm achieves sublinear regret, meaning average regret goes to zero over time. Experience replay — storing and re-sampling past tasks — helps prevent catastrophic forgetting when adapting to new tasks. Adaptive learning rates that respond to recent task performance enable the algorithm to learn quickly on easy tasks and carefully on difficult ones. Online meta-learning is essential for real-world applications where data arrives as a stream and the model must continuously improve without full retraining.
